\section{Introduction}

\subsection{The question}

Fix a monic irreducible $f\in\mathbb{Z}[x]$ of degree $n$, let $K=\mathbb{Q}[x]/(f)$ with Galois
closure $L$ and group $G=\mathrm{Gal}(L/\mathbb{Q})\le S_n$. For each prime $p\nmid\disc(f)$, the
degrees of the irreducible factors of $f$ modulo $p$ form a partition $T(p)\vdash n$, equal to the
cycle type of the Frobenius conjugacy class $\mathrm{Frob}_p\subseteq G$.

Chebotarev's density theorem says that $\mathrm{Frob}_p$ equidistributes over conjugacy classes: the
density of primes with $\mathrm{Frob}_p$ in a class $\mathcal{C}$ is $\abs{\mathcal{C}}/\abs{G}$. Thus
$T$ is, in the density sense, the cycle type of a uniformly random element of $G$.

Some information about $T$ is available cheaply, as a congruence on $p$. The classical instance is
the discriminant character: $\left(\frac{\disc f}{p}\right)=\sgn(\mathrm{Frob}_p)$, and by quadratic
reciprocity the left-hand side depends only on $p$ modulo $\abs{\disc f}$. More generally, class
field theory identifies the read-outs of $\mathrm{Frob}_p$ determined by congruences on $p$ with those
factoring through the abelianization $G^{\ab}=G/[G,G]$. The question of this paper is: \emph{how many
bits of the splitting type are congruence-visible?}

\subsection{The answer}

Exactly $\log_2\abs{G^{\ab}}$; and this is a ceiling for all congruence read-outs simultaneously.
For $G=S_n$ this is one bit for every $n\ge 2$, while $H(T)$ grows without bound, so the visible
fraction tends to $0$. For abelian $G$ it is $\log_2\abs{G}$: everything. For a perfect group it is
$0$: nothing.

\section{The counting-entropy calculus}

Throughout, $s$ is a nonempty finite set (in the application, the group $G$) with the uniform
measure, and a \emph{read-out} is any function on $s$ with values in a set with decidable equality.

\begin{definition}[Uniform entropy]
For a read-out $g$ write $s_g(a)=\{x\in s: g(x)=g(a)\}$. Then
\[
  H_s(g)\;=\;\log_2\abs{s}\;-\;\frac1{\abs{s}}\sum_{a\in s}\log_2\abs{s_g(a)} .
\]
Grouping by fibres shows that if the distinct values of $g$ have fibres of sizes $n_1,\dots,n_r$
with $\sum n_i=N=\abs{s}$, then $H_s(g)=-\sum_i \frac{n_i}{N}\log_2\frac{n_i}{N}$, Shannon's entropy
of the pushforward.
\end{definition}

\begin{definition}[Conditional entropy and mutual information]
$H_s(g\mid k)=\sum_{v\in k(s)}\frac{\abs{k^{-1}(v)}}{\abs{s}}H_{k^{-1}(v)}(g)$ and
$I_s(g;k)=H_s(g)-H_s(g\mid k)$.
\end{definition}

\begin{lemma}[Constancy]\label{lem:const}
If $g$ is constant on $s$ then $H(g)=0$.
\end{lemma}
\begin{proof}
Every fibre equals $s$, so every summand $\log_2\abs{s}-\log_2\abs{s}$ vanishes.
\end{proof}

\begin{theorem}[Chain rule]\label{thm:chain}
$H(g\mid k)=H\big((g,k)\big)-H(k)$, where $(g,k)$ is the joint read-out $x\mapsto (g(x),k(x))$.
\end{theorem}
\begin{proof}[Proof sketch]
The fibre of $(g,k)$ through $x$ is the fibre of $g$ computed inside the fibre of $k$ through $x$.
Writing each entropy as $\log_2$ of a cardinality minus an average of logarithms of fibre
cardinalities and regrouping the double sum over the fibres of $k$ makes the identity telescope.
\end{proof}

\begin{corollary}[Symmetry]\label{cor:sym}
$I(g;k)=I(k;g)$.
\end{corollary}
\begin{proof}
By Theorem~\ref{thm:chain} both sides equal $H(g)+H(k)-H((g,k))$, the joint read-out being
insensitive to the order of its components.
\end{proof}

Symmetry is the engine of the paper: it converts the hard direction (``how much does a character
tell you about the splitting type?'') into the trivial one (``how much does the splitting type tell
you about the character?'').

\begin{lemma}[Non-negativity and the cap]\label{lem:cap}
$H(g\mid k)\ge 0$; hence $I(g;k)\le H(g)$ and, by symmetry, $I(g;k)\le H(k)$.
\end{lemma}

\begin{lemma}[Post-processing]\label{lem:pp}
$H(u\circ k)\le H(k)$ for any map $u$.
\end{lemma}
\begin{proof}[Proof sketch]
Each fibre of $u\circ k$ is a union of fibres of $k$; the entropy formula decreases as fibres grow.
This is the data-processing inequality for a deterministic channel.
\end{proof}

\begin{lemma}[Refinement kills conditional entropy]\label{lem:ref}
If $g(x)=g(y)\Rightarrow k(x)=k(y)$ for all $x,y\in s$, then $H(k\mid g)=0$.
\end{lemma}
\begin{proof}
On each fibre of $g$ the read-out $k$ is constant; apply Lemma~\ref{lem:const} and average.
\end{proof}

\begin{lemma}[Strict positivity]\label{lem:pos}
If $k(x)\ne k(y)$ for some $x,y\in s$ then $H(k)>0$. If moreover $g(x)=g(y)$ while $k(x)\ne k(y)$
(a \emph{mixed fibre}), then $H(k\mid g)>0$.
\end{lemma}
\begin{proof}[Proof sketch]
A fibre of $k$ is then a proper nonempty subset, so some term of the entropy sum is strictly
positive while all terms are non-negative; for the conditional statement apply the same argument
inside the fibre of $g$ containing $x$ and $y$, whose weight is positive.
\end{proof}

\section{Balanced read-outs}

\begin{theorem}[A balanced $m$-valued read-out carries exactly $\log_2 m$ bits]\label{thm:bal}
Let $m\ge 1$ and suppose $m\cdot\abs{s_k(a)}=\abs{s}$ for all $a\in s$. Then $H(k)=\log_2 m$.
\end{theorem}
\begin{proof}
For each $a$, $\log_2\abs{s_k(a)}=\log_2\abs{s}-\log_2 m$; averaging a constant returns it, so
$H(k)=\log_2\abs{s}-(\log_2\abs{s}-\log_2 m)=\log_2 m$.
\end{proof}

\begin{theorem}[One bit from a balanced binary refinement]\label{thm:onebit}
Let $k$ satisfy $2\abs{s_k(a)}=\abs{s}$ for all $a$, and let $g$ refine $k$. Then
\[
  I(g;k)=1,\qquad H(g\mid k)=H(g)-1 .
\]
\end{theorem}
\begin{proof}
By Corollary~\ref{cor:sym}, $I(g;k)=H(k)-H(k\mid g)$. Lemma~\ref{lem:ref} gives $H(k\mid g)=0$ and
Theorem~\ref{thm:bal} gives $H(k)=1$. The second identity rearranges
$I(g;k)=H(g)-H(g\mid k)$.
\end{proof}

Nothing is assumed about the richness of $g$: however fine the read-out, exactly one bit passes.

\section{The abelian ceiling}

Let $G$ be a finite group with the uniform measure and let $\cl:G\to \mathrm{ConjClasses}(G)$,
$\sigma\mapsto[\sigma]$, be the conjugacy-class read-out --- the complete arithmetic datum attached
to an unramified prime by Chebotarev.

\begin{lemma}[Fibres of a surjective character]\label{lem:fib}
If $\chi:G\to C$ is a surjective homomorphism of finite groups, every fibre of $\chi$ has exactly
$\abs{G}/\abs{C}$ elements.
\end{lemma}
\begin{proof}
Fibres are cosets of $\ker\chi$, hence equinumerous; partitioning $G$ into the $\abs{C}$ nonempty
fibres gives $\abs{G}=\abs{C}\cdot\abs{\ker\chi}$.
\end{proof}

\begin{corollary}\label{cor:Hchi}
$H(\chi)=\log_2\abs{C}$ for a surjective character $\chi:G\to C$.
\end{corollary}

\begin{lemma}[Abelian characters are class functions]\label{lem:classfn}
If $C$ is abelian and $\chi:G\to C$ is a homomorphism, then
$\chi(cxc^{-1})=\chi(c)\chi(x)\chi(c)^{-1}=\chi(x)$. Hence $\cl$ always refines $\chi$.
\end{lemma}

\begin{theorem}[Exact visible information]\label{thm:exact}
Let $G$ be a finite group, $C$ a finite abelian group and $\chi:G\to C$ a surjective homomorphism.
Then
\[
  I\big(\cl;\chi\big)\;=\;\log_2\abs{C}.
\]
\end{theorem}
\begin{proof}
By symmetry $I(\cl;\chi)=H(\chi)-H(\chi\mid\cl)$. Lemma~\ref{lem:classfn} and Lemma~\ref{lem:ref}
give $H(\chi\mid\cl)=0$; Corollary~\ref{cor:Hchi} gives $H(\chi)=\log_2\abs{C}$.
\end{proof}

\begin{theorem}[The exact deficit]\label{thm:deficit}
Under the same hypotheses, $H(\cl\mid\chi)=H(\cl)-\log_2\abs{C}$.
\end{theorem}

\begin{theorem}[The abelian ceiling]\label{thm:ceiling}
Let $\chi:G\to C$ be a surjective character onto a finite abelian group and let $u$ be an arbitrary
map defined on $C$. Then
\[
  I\big(\cl;u\circ\chi\big)\;\le\;\log_2\abs{C},
\]
with equality for $u=\mathrm{id}$.
\end{theorem}
\begin{proof}
By Lemma~\ref{lem:cap}, $I(\cl;u\circ\chi)\le H(u\circ\chi)$; by Lemma~\ref{lem:pp},
$H(u\circ\chi)\le H(\chi)$; by Corollary~\ref{cor:Hchi}, $H(\chi)=\log_2\abs{C}$. Attainment is
Theorem~\ref{thm:exact}.
\end{proof}

\begin{corollary}[Index-two quotient: exactly one bit]\label{cor:onebit}
If $\abs{C}=2$ then $I(\cl;\chi)=1$, and every read-out factoring through $\chi$ satisfies $I\le 1$.
\end{corollary}

\subsection{Arithmetic interpretation}

Take $C=G^{\ab}$ with $\chi$ the canonical surjection. By the Artin reciprocity law the maximal
abelian subextension of $L/\mathbb{Q}$ has group $G^{\ab}$ and lies in a cyclotomic field
$\mathbb{Q}(\zeta_N)$, $N$ the conductor; the image of $\mathrm{Frob}_p$ in $G^{\ab}$ is a function of
$p\bmod N$, and conversely every congruence-determined read-out of $\mathrm{Frob}_p$ factors through
$G^{\ab}$. Theorem~\ref{thm:ceiling} therefore says: \emph{no congruence condition on $p$, of any
modulus, reveals more than $\log_2\abs{G^{\ab}}$ bits about the splitting type of $p$, and the
canonical character attains this bound.}

\begin{corollary}[Abelian fields hide nothing]\label{cor:abelian}
If $G$ is abelian, take $\chi=\mathrm{id}_G$. Conjugacy classes are singletons and
$I(\cl;\chi)=\log_2\abs{G}=H(\cl)$: the residue determines the splitting completely, and the deficit
of Theorem~\ref{thm:deficit} vanishes. This is quadratic reciprocity, and its cyclotomic
generalization, read information-theoretically.
\end{corollary}

\section{The $S_3$ cubic $x^3+x+1$, discriminant $-31$}

\subsection{Setup}

The polynomial $f(x)=x^3+x+1$ is irreducible over $\mathbb{Q}$ with discriminant
$-4\cdot 1^3-27\cdot 1^2=-31$, squarefree and negative, so $G=S_3$. Define the \emph{splitting type}
of $\sigma\in S_3$ as its cycle type padded by fixed points,
\[
  T(\sigma)=\text{cycle type of }\sigma+\underbrace{1+\cdots+1}_{3-\abs{\supp(\sigma)}},
\]
a partition of $3$. Its image is $\{\texttt{111},\texttt{12},\texttt{3}\}$ with fibre sizes
$1$, $3$, $2$ out of $6$: the Chebotarev densities $1/6$, $1/2$, $1/3$.

The quadratic character $\left(\frac{-31}{p}\right)$ equals the sign of the Frobenius permutation,
and as a function of the type
\[
  \sgn=\varepsilon\circ T,\qquad
  \varepsilon(t)=\begin{cases}-1,& t=\texttt{12},\\ +1,& t\in\{\texttt{111},\texttt{3}\}.\end{cases}
\]
That the sign factors through the type is the only arithmetic input below.

\subsection{The two entropies}

\begin{proposition}[Type entropy]\label{prop:HT}
$H(T)=\tfrac23+\tfrac{\log_2 3}{2}=1.4591\ldots$
\end{proposition}
\begin{proof}
With $N=6$ and fibre sizes $1,3,2$,
$H(T)=\log_2 6-\tfrac16(\log_2 1+3\log_2 3+2\log_2 2)=1+\log_2 3-\tfrac{\log_2 3}{2}-\tfrac13$.
\end{proof}

\begin{theorem}[Exactly one bit]\label{thm:S3}
$I(T;\sgn)=1$.
\end{theorem}
\begin{proof}
The sign is balanced on $S_3$ (three odd, three even elements) and $T$ refines it because
$\sgn=\varepsilon\circ T$. Apply Theorem~\ref{thm:onebit}; alternatively Theorem~\ref{thm:exact}
with $C=\{\pm1\}$.
\end{proof}

\begin{corollary}[The locked residual]\label{cor:res}
$H(T\mid\sgn)=H(T)-1=\tfrac{\log_2 3}{2}-\tfrac13=0.4591\ldots$
\end{corollary}

\begin{proposition}[Decomposition]\label{prop:decomp}
$H(T\mid\sgn)=\tfrac12\big(\log_2 3-\tfrac23\big)=\tfrac12 H\!\left(\tfrac13,\tfrac23\right)$.
\end{proposition}
\begin{proof}
The odd fibre (three transpositions) is pure of type $\texttt{12}$ and contributes $0$; the even
fibre (identity and two $3$-cycles) has type distribution $(\tfrac13,\tfrac23)$ with entropy
$\log_2 3-\tfrac23$. Each fibre has weight $\tfrac12$.
\end{proof}

\subsection{Numerical brackets}

The rational sandwich $\frac{84}{53}<\log_2 3<\frac{65}{41}$ --- equivalent to the finite integer
computations $3^{53}>2^{84}$ and $3^{41}<2^{65}$ --- yields
\[
  1.4591<H(T)<1.4594,\qquad 0.4591<H(T\mid\sgn)<0.4594 .
\]
In particular $H(T\mid\sgn)>0$: the residual is strictly positive, the channel is strictly lossy
($I=1<H(T)$), and the visible fraction is $1/H(T)=68.5\ldots\%$.

\subsection{Mixed-type residue classes are forced}

An empirical scan of primes by residue modulo $31$ finds that $15$ of the residue classes host two
distinct splitting types: both $\texttt{111}$ and $\texttt{3}$ occur. This is what the theory
demands. The character separates only even from odd; within the even class of $S_3$ the counts are
$1$ (identity, type $\texttt{111}$) against $2$ (three-cycles, type $\texttt{3}$), a $1:2$ split
identical for every even residue class. Formally, there exist $\sigma,\tau$ with
$\sgn(\sigma)=\sgn(\tau)$ but $T(\sigma)\ne T(\tau)$. Pure residue classes throughout would force
$H(T\mid\sgn)=0$, contradicting Corollary~\ref{cor:res}. The $15$ mixed classes are exactly the $15$
classes with $\left(\frac{-31}{p}\right)=+1$: a countable manifestation of the $0.4591$ hidden bits.

\section{Strictness: the result is about the type}

\begin{definition}
Let $\mathrm{sc}:S_3\to\{\text{true},\text{false}\}$ be the coarse read-out ``does $p$ split
completely?'', i.e.\ $\mathrm{sc}(\sigma)=[\,T(\sigma)=\texttt{111}\,]$.
\end{definition}

\begin{proposition}[A mixed fibre]\label{prop:mixed}
A transposition and a three-cycle have the same value of $\mathrm{sc}$ but opposite signs.
\end{proposition}

\begin{theorem}[Coarsening strictly loses]\label{thm:strict}
$I(\mathrm{sc};\sgn)<1=I(T;\sgn)$.
\end{theorem}
\begin{proof}
By symmetry $I(\mathrm{sc};\sgn)=1-H(\sgn\mid\mathrm{sc})$, and Proposition~\ref{prop:mixed} with
Lemma~\ref{lem:pos} gives $H(\sgn\mid\mathrm{sc})>0$.
\end{proof}

Numerically $\mathrm{sc}$ has fibre sizes $1$ and $5$, the large fibre containing $3$ odd and $2$
even elements, so $I(\mathrm{sc};\sgn)=1-\tfrac56 H(\tfrac35,\tfrac25)=0.1908\ldots$ bits. The full
splitting type strictly beats its natural coarsening.

\section{Symmetric groups and the general landscape}

\begin{theorem}[One bit for every symmetric group]\label{thm:Sn}
For every finite set with at least two points, the cycle type of a uniformly random permutation and
its sign satisfy $I(\text{cycle type};\sgn)=1$ and
$H(\text{cycle type}\mid\sgn)=H(\text{cycle type})-1$.
\end{theorem}
\begin{proof}
The sign is a surjective homomorphism onto a two-element group, hence balanced by
Lemma~\ref{lem:fib}, and it is a function of the cycle type. Apply Theorem~\ref{thm:onebit}.
\end{proof}

\begin{corollary}
No read-out of a permutation, however fine, extracts more than one bit about the sign.
\end{corollary}

The cycle-type distribution on $S_n$ is the Ewens measure at parameter $1$, $\Pr[\lambda]=1/z_\lambda$
with $z_\lambda=\prod_i i^{m_i}m_i!$, and $H(T)=\Theta(\log n)$; the hidden residual $H(T)-1$
diverges. For $n=3,4,5,6$ one finds $H(T)=1.4591,\,2.0944,\,2.5573,\,3.0353$ bits, with visible
fractions $68.5\%$, $47.8\%$, $39.1\%$, $33.0\%$.

\centering

\toprule
Galois group $G$ & $G^{\ab}$ & visible bits & hidden bits\\
\midrule
abelian & $G$ & $\log_2\abs{G}$ (all) & $0$\\
$S_n$, $n\ge 2$ & $C_2$ & $1$ & $H(T)-1\to\infty$\\
$A_n$, $n\ge5$ (perfect) & trivial & $0$ & $H(T)$ (all)\\
general $G$ & $G/[G,G]$ & $\log_2\abs{G^{\ab}}$ & $H(\cl)-\log_2\abs{G^{\ab}}$\\
\bottomrule
\end{tabular}
\caption{Congruence-visible and hidden Frobenius information.}
\end{table}

\section{Algorithms}

\paragraph{Exact channel evaluation.} Given a finite group $G$ and read-outs $g,k$, partition $G$ by
$k$, compute the entropy of $g$ within each block, average with block weights and subtract: this
returns $H(g)$, $H(k)$, $H(g\mid k)$ and $I(g;k)$ in $O(\abs{G})$ hash operations. For $S_3$ with
$g=T$, $k=\sgn$ it returns $1.4591\ldots$, $1$, $0.4591\ldots$, $1$.

\paragraph{The ceiling certificate.} Given a surjective $\chi:G\to C$ with $C$ abelian, verify in
$O(\abs{G})$ that all fibres have size $\abs{G}/\abs{C}$ and that $\chi$ is a class function; then
$\log_2\abs{C}$ is a certified upper bound for $I(\cl;w)$ over \emph{all} post-processings
$w=u\circ\chi$, of which there are Bell-many. The certificate replaces an exponential search by a
linear check.

\paragraph{Residue-stratified Chebotarev scan.} Given a monic integer cubic $f$, a bound $X$ and
$N=\abs{\disc f}$, compute for each prime $p\le X$ its splitting type (for a cubic: three roots
$\Rightarrow\texttt{111}$, one root $\Rightarrow\texttt{12}$, none $\Rightarrow\texttt{3}$) and
tabulate by $p\bmod N$. The empirical mutual information converges to $1$, and the table exhibits
the $15$ mixed classes.

\section{Discussion}

The theorem is a conservation law for arithmetic information. The Frobenius class carries $H(\cl)$
bits; class field theory makes an abelian portion legible as congruences; the size of the legible
portion is neither ``most'' nor ``asymptotically negligible'' but precisely $\log_2\abs{G^{\ab}}$, a
quantity blind to everything about $G$ except its abelianization. The proof is short and structural:
symmetry of mutual information puts the trivial direction on top, and the fact that abelian
characters are class functions supplies the required refinement for free.

Abelian class field theory asserts that the $\log_2\abs{G^{\ab}}$ bits \emph{are} available; the
ceiling is the converse, that nothing else is. The non-abelian residual is what the Langlands
program addresses by replacing congruences with automorphic coefficients: for the cubic of
discriminant $-31$ the remaining $0.4591$ bits are supplied by the coefficients $a_p$ of the
weight-one cusp form attached to the associated two-dimensional Galois representation, which
separates the identity class from the three-cycles by $a_p=2$ versus $a_p=-1$.

Three caveats. The measure is the exact Chebotarev measure, so finite scans approximate the
theorems with an error governed by effective Chebotarev bounds. We quantify information about the
conjugacy class, which coincides with the cycle type for $S_n$ but is finer in general --- the
ceiling nevertheless holds for all read-outs. And all entropies are one-prime quantities.

Finally, the cancellation $1.4591\ldots-0.4591\ldots=1$ is not an accident of small numbers. Both
quantities contain $\tfrac{\log_2 3}{2}$ because both measure the same biased $1:2$ coin inside the
even class; the character learns nothing about that coin, so it cancels, leaving the balanced coin
the character does see. The exact integer is the arithmetic shadow of the exact sequence
$1\to A_3\to S_3\to C_2\to 1$.

\section{Future work}

\paragraph{Equality-case rigidity.} The ceiling proof factors as
$I\le H(w)\le H(\chi)=\log_2\abs{C}$, with equality in each step exactly when a conditional entropy
vanishes. We conjecture $I(\cl;w)=\log_2\abs{C}$ holds iff $w$ separates the fibres of $\chi$, i.e.\
the ceiling is attained only by read-outs from which the character can be recovered. Missing is a
quantitative gap $\log_2\abs{C}-I\ge c\cdot(\text{defect})$, which should follow from strict
concavity of $-p\log p$ rather than from arithmetic.

\paragraph{Closed form for the $S_n$ residual.} For all $n\ge2$ the residual is $H(T)-1$ with
$H(T)=\log_2 n!-\frac1{n!}\sum_{\lambda\vdash n}\frac{n!}{z_\lambda}\log_2\frac{n!}{z_\lambda}$; a
closed form and the growth rate $\Theta(\log n)$ would quantify the divergence of hidden
information.

\paragraph{Multiplicativity over composita.} For fields with coprime discriminants and groups
$G_1,G_2$ we expect $I=\log_2\abs{G_1^{\ab}}+\log_2\abs{G_2^{\ab}}$ for the compositum, since
$(G_1\times G_2)^{\ab}=G_1^{\ab}\times G_2^{\ab}$: visible information is additive while total type
entropy is subadditive, so the hidden fraction grows.

\paragraph{Noisy read-outs and higher moments.} Replacing $u\circ\chi$ by a Markov kernel should
preserve the ceiling via the data-processing inequality, with equality becoming a statement about
sufficient statistics; and large-deviation rates for the log-likelihood ratio between
residue-conditional and unconditional type distributions would sharpen empirical scans.

\section{Conclusion}

For the cubic field of discriminant $-31$ the quadratic character captures exactly one bit of the
$1.4591\ldots$ bits of splitting-type entropy, leaving $0.4591\ldots$ bits locked behind the
non-abelian structure of $S_3$. The one is $\log_2 2$ and $2=\abs{S_3^{\ab}}$: the coincidence is a
theorem. For any finite group and any surjective character onto a finite abelian group $C$, the
Frobenius class and the character share exactly $\log_2\abs{C}$ bits, every read-out computable from
the character is capped at that value, and the deficit is exactly $H(\cl)-\log_2\abs{C}$. Abelian
Galois groups hide nothing; symmetric groups hide everything but one bit.

"""
The abelian ceiling: exactly log2 |G^ab| bits of Frobenius information
are visible in a residue.

This self-contained script demonstrates, numerically and by exhaustive
enumeration, every quantitative claim of the accompanying paper:

  1. The Chebotarev channel of the cubic field x^3 + x + 1 (discriminant -31,
     Galois group S_3):  H(T) = 2/3 + (log2 3)/2 = 1.4591...,
     H(T | sign) = (log2 3)/2 - 1/3 = 0.4591..., I(T ; sign) = 1 EXACTLY.

  2. The decomposition H(T | sign) = (1/2) * H(1/3, 2/3):  the odd half of the
     group is pure, the even half splits 1 : 2.

  3. The abelian ceiling: for every surjective character chi : G -> C onto a
     finite abelian group, I(conjugacy class ; chi) = log2 |C|, and every
     post-processing u . chi satisfies I <= log2 |C| (checked by brute-force
     enumeration of ALL set partitions of C).

  4. The dichotomy: an abelian Galois group hides nothing (I = log2 |G|);
     a symmetric group leaks exactly one bit for every n >= 2.

  5. An honest arithmetic scan: factorization types of x^3 + x + 1 modulo the
     primes, stratified by residue mod 31, exhibiting the 15 mixed-type
     residue classes forced by the theory.

Run:  python3 demo.py
Only the standard library is used.
"""

from __future__ import annotations

from collections import Counter, defaultdict
from itertools import permutations
from math import log2
from typing import Callable, Dict, Hashable, Iterable, List, Sequence, Tuple

Perm = Tuple[int, ...]
Readout = Callable[[Perm], Hashable]


# ----------------------------------------------------------------------
# 1. The counting-entropy calculus (uniform / Chebotarev measure)
# ----------------------------------------------------------------------

def entropy_of_counts(counts: Iterable[int]) -> float:
    """Shannon entropy in bits of the distribution proportional to `counts`."""
    cs: List[int] = [c for c in counts if c > 0]
    total: int = sum(cs)
    if total == 0:
        return 0.0
    return -sum((c / total) * log2(c / total) for c in cs)


def uniform_entropy(domain: Sequence[Hashable], g: Callable[[Hashable], Hashable]) -> float:
    """H(g) for the uniform measure on `domain`."""
    return entropy_of_counts(Counter(g(x) for x in domain).values())


def conditional_entropy(
    domain: Sequence[Hashable],
    g: Callable[[Hashable], Hashable],
    k: Callable[[Hashable], Hashable],
) -> float:
    """H(g | k): the average entropy of g over the fibres of k."""
    blocks: Dict[Hashable, List[Hashable]] = defaultdict(list)
    for x in domain:
        blocks[k(x)].append(x)
    n: int = len(domain)
    return sum((len(b) / n) * uniform_entropy(b, g) for b in blocks.values())


def mutual_information(
    domain: Sequence[Hashable],
    g: Callable[[Hashable], Hashable],
    k: Callable[[Hashable], Hashable],
) -> float:
    """I(g ; k) = H(g) - H(g | k)."""
    return uniform_entropy(domain, g) - conditional_entropy(domain, g, k)


# ----------------------------------------------------------------------
# 2. Permutation groups, cycle types, signs, conjugacy classes
# ----------------------------------------------------------------------

def symmetric_group(n: int) -> List[Perm]:
    """All permutations of {0,...,n-1}, as tuples p with i |-> p[i]."""
    return [tuple(p) for p in permutations(range(n))]


def cycle_type(p: Perm) -> Tuple[int, ...]:
    """Cycle type of p as a weakly decreasing tuple (a partition of n)."""
    n: int = len(p)
    seen: List[bool] = [False] * n
    parts: List[int] = []
    for i in range(n):
        if not seen[i]:
            length, j = 0, i
            while not seen[j]:
                seen[j] = True
                j = p[j]
                length += 1
            parts.append(length)
    return tuple(sorted(parts, reverse=True))


def sign(p: Perm) -> int:
    """Sign of a permutation: +1 if even, -1 if odd."""
    ct: Tuple[int, ...] = cycle_type(p)
    return (-1) ** sum(length - 1 for length in ct)


def conj_class(p: Perm) -> Tuple[int, ...]:
    """For a symmetric group, the conjugacy class is exactly the cycle type."""
    return cycle_type(p)


def type_label(ct: Tuple[int, ...]) -> str:
    """'111', '12', '3', ... — the classical splitting-type notation."""
    return "".join(str(part) for part in sorted(ct))


# ----------------------------------------------------------------------
# 3. Demonstration 1 — the S_3 cubic x^3 + x + 1, discriminant -31
# ----------------------------------------------------------------------

def demo_s3_channel() -> None:
    print("=" * 72)
    print("1. THE CUBIC x^3 + x + 1,  disc = -31,  Galois group S_3")
    print("=" * 72)

    G: List[Perm] = symmetric_group(3)
    counts: Counter = Counter(type_label(cycle_type(p)) for p in G)
    print("\nChebotarev densities (fraction of the group per splitting type):")
    for label in ("111", "12", "3"):
        print(f"   type {label:>3} : {counts[label]}/6 = {counts[label] / 6:.6f}")

    H_T: float = uniform_entropy(G, lambda p: cycle_type(p))
    H_sign: float = uniform_entropy(G, sign)
    H_T_given_sign: float = conditional_entropy(G, lambda p: cycle_type(p), sign)
    I: float = mutual_information(G, lambda p: cycle_type(p), sign)

    exact_H_T: float = 2 / 3 + log2(3) / 2
    exact_res: float = log2(3) / 2 - 1 / 3

    print(f"\n   H(T)              = {H_T:.10f}   (exact 2/3 + (log2 3)/2 = {exact_H_T:.10f})")
    print(f"   H(sign)           = {H_sign:.10f}   (a fair coin: 3 odd, 3 even)")
    print(f"   H(T | sign)       = {H_T_given_sign:.10f}   (exact (log2 3)/2 - 1/3 = {exact_res:.10f})")
    print(f"   I(T ; sign)       = {I:.10f}   <-- EXACTLY ONE BIT")
    print(f"   visible fraction  = {I / H_T:.4%}")

    assert abs(I - 1.0) < 1e-12
    assert abs(H_T - exact_H_T) < 1e-12
    assert abs(H_T_given_sign - exact_res) < 1e-12

    # symmetry of mutual information: the trivial direction
    H_sign_given_T: float = conditional_entropy(G, sign, lambda p: cycle_type(p))
    print(f"\n   H(sign | T)       = {H_sign_given_T:.10f}   (the sign IS a function of the type)")
    print("   hence  I(T ; sign) = I(sign ; T) = H(sign) - 0 = 1.")
    assert abs(H_sign_given_T) < 1e-12

    # the paper's decomposition
    half_binary: float = 0.5 * entropy_of_counts([1, 2])
    print(f"\n   Decomposition:  (1/2) * H(1/3, 2/3) = {half_binary:.10f}")
    print("   the odd half is pure (all type '12'); the even half splits 1 : 2.")
    assert abs(H_T_given_sign - half_binary) < 1e-12

    # strictness: a coarser read-out loses
    splits_completely: Readout = lambda p: cycle_type(p) == (1, 1, 1)
    I_coarse: float = mutual_information(G, splits_completely, sign)
    print(f"\n   Coarse read-out 'does p split completely?':  I = {I_coarse:.10f} < 1")
    print("   so the one-bit value is a property of the splitting type, not of the framework.")
    assert I_coarse < 1 - 1e-9


# ----------------------------------------------------------------------
# 4. Demonstration 2 — the abelian ceiling, verified by brute force
# ----------------------------------------------------------------------

def set_partitions(items: Sequence[Hashable]) -> Iterable[List[List[Hashable]]]:
    """All set partitions of `items` (Bell-number many)."""
    if not items:
        yield []
        return
    first, rest = items[0], items[1:]
    for partition in set_partitions(rest):
        for i in range(len(partition)):
            yield partition[:i] + [[first] + partition[i]] + partition[i + 1:]
        yield [[first]] + partition


def demo_abelian_ceiling(n: int = 4) -> None:
    print()
    print("=" * 72)
    print(f"2. THE ABELIAN CEILING for G = S_{n},  chi = sign,  C = {{+1,-1}}")
    print("=" * 72)

    G: List[Perm] = symmetric_group(n)
    ceiling: float = log2(2)

    I_exact: float = mutual_information(G, conj_class, sign)
    print(f"\n   I(conjugacy class ; sign) = {I_exact:.10f}   = log2 |C| = {ceiling:.10f}")
    assert abs(I_exact - ceiling) < 1e-12

    H_class: float = uniform_entropy(G, conj_class)

def primes_up_to(limit: int) -> List[int]:
    """Sieve of Eratosthenes."""
    sieve: List[bool] = [True] * (limit + 1)
    sieve[0:2] = [False, False]
    for i in range(2, int(limit ** 0.5) + 1):
        if sieve[i]:
            for j in range(i * i, limit + 1, i):
                sieve[j] = False
    return [i for i, is_p in enumerate(sieve) if is_p]


def splitting_type_of_cubic(p: int) -> str:
    """
    Splitting type of x^3 + x + 1 modulo p, for p not dividing 31.

    A cubic over a finite field is determined by its number of roots:
      3 roots -> '111' (splits completely), 1 root -> '12', 0 roots -> '3'.
    """
    roots: int = sum(1 for x in range(p) if (x * x * x + x + 1) % p == 0)
    if roots == 3:
        return "111"
    if roots == 1:
        return "12"
    return "3"


def legendre_symbol(a: int, p: int) -> int:
    """The Legendre symbol (a|p) by Euler's criterion, p an odd prime."""
    a %= p
    if a == 0:
        return 0
    r: int = pow(a, (p - 1) // 2, p)
    return 1 if r == 1 else -1

    mismatches: int = sum(

Perm = Tuple[int, ...]
Readout = Callable[[Perm], Hashable]


# ----------------------------------------------------------------------
# 1. The counting-entropy calculus (uniform / Chebotarev measure)
# ----------------------------------------------------------------------

def entropy_of_counts(counts: Iterable[int]) -> float:
    """Shannon entropy in bits of the distribution proportional to `counts`."""
    cs: List[int] = [c for c in counts if c > 0]
    total: int = sum(cs)
    if total == 0:
        return 0.0
    return -sum((c / total) * log2(c / total) for c in cs)


def uniform_entropy(domain: Sequence[Hashable], g: Callable[[Hashable], Hashable]) -> float:
    """H(g) for the uniform measure on `domain`."""
    return entropy_of_counts(Counter(g(x) for x in domain).values())


def conditional_entropy(
    domain: Sequence[Hashable],
    g: Callable[[Hashable], Hashable],
    k: Callable[[Hashable], Hashable],
) -> float:
    """H(g | k): the average entropy of g over the fibres of k."""
    blocks: Dict[Hashable, List[Hashable]] = defaultdict(list)
    for x in domain:
        blocks[k(x)].append(x)
    n: int = len(domain)
    return sum((len(b) / n) * uniform_entropy(b, g) for b in blocks.values())


def mutual_information(
    domain: Sequence[Hashable],
    g: Callable[[Hashable], Hashable],
    k: Callable[[Hashable], Hashable],
) -> float:
    """I(g ; k) = H(g) - H(g | k)."""
    return uniform_entropy(domain, g) - conditional_entropy(domain, g, k)

# 2. Permutation groups, cycle types, signs, conjugacy classes
# ----------------------------------------------------------------------

def symmetric_group(n: int) -> List[Perm]:
    """All permutations of {0,...,n-1}, as tuples p with i |-> p[i]."""
    return [tuple(p) for p in permutations(range(n))]


def cycle_type(p: Perm) -> Tuple[int, ...]:
    """Cycle type of p as a weakly decreasing tuple (a partition of n)."""
    n: int = len(p)
    seen: List[bool] = [False] * n
    parts: List[int] = []
    for i in range(n):
        if not seen[i]:
            length, j = 0, i
            while not seen[j]:
                seen[j] = True
                j = p[j]
                length += 1
            parts.append(length)
    return tuple(sorted(parts, reverse=True))


def sign(p: Perm) -> int:
    """Sign of a permutation: +1 if even, -1 if odd."""
    ct: Tuple[int, ...] = cycle_type(p)
    return (-1) ** sum(length - 1 for length in ct)


def conj_class(p: Perm) -> Tuple[int, ...]:
    """For a symmetric group, the conjugacy class is exactly the cycle type."""
    return cycle_type(p)


def type_label(ct: Tuple[int, ...]) -> str:
    """'111', '12', '3', ... — the classical splitting-type notation."""
    return "".join(str(part) for part in sorted(ct))

def set_partitions(items: Sequence[Hashable]) -> Iterable[List[List[Hashable]]]:
    """All set partitions of `items` (Bell-number many)."""
    if not items:
        yield []
        return
    first, rest = items[0], items[1:]
    for partition in set_partitions(rest):
        for i in range(len(partition)):
            yield partition[:i] + [[first] + partition[i]] + partition[i + 1:]
        yield [[first]] + partition

from __future__ import annotations

from collections import defaultdict
from math import log2

def entropy_of_counts(counts: Iterable[int]) -> float:

    cs: List[int] = [c for c in counts if c > 0]
    total: int = sum(cs)

    return -sum((c / total) * log2(c / total) for c in cs)


def fibres(

    H_k: float = entropy_of_counts(len(b) for b in fibres(domain, k).values())

from __future__ import annotations

from collections import defaultdict
from math import log2
from typing import Dict, List, Sequence, Tuple


def conjugacy_classes(mul: Sequence[Sequence[int]], inv: Sequence[int]) -> List[List[int]]:
    """Conjugacy classes of the group given by its multiplication table."""
    n: int = len(mul)
    label: List[int] = [-1] * n
    classes: List[List[int]] = []
    for x in range(n):
        if label[x] >= 0:
            continue
        block: List[int] = sorted({mul[mul[c][x]][inv[c]] for c in range(n)})
        idx: int = len(classes)
        for y in block:
            label[y] = idx
        classes.append(block)
    return classes


def certify_abelian_ceiling(
    mul: Sequence[Sequence[int]],
    inv: Sequence[int],
    chi: Sequence[int],
    card_C: int,
) -> Dict[str, object]:
    """Verify the ceiling hypotheses and return the certified bound log2 |C|."""
    n: int = len(mul)

    fibre_sizes: Dict[int, int] = defaultdict(int)
    for x in range(n):
        fibre_sizes[chi[x]] += 1
    surjective: bool = len(fibre_sizes) == card_C
    balanced: bool = all(card_C * size == n for size in fibre_sizes.values())

    # The consequence of abelian-valued homomorphy that the theorem uses:
    # chi is constant on conjugacy classes.
    class_function: bool = all(
        len({chi[y] for y in block}) == 1 for block in conjugacy_classes(mul, inv)
    )

    H_class: float = _entropy([len(b) for b in conjugacy_classes(mul, inv)])
    ceiling: float = log2(card_C)
    return {
        "surjective": surjective,
        "balanced_fibres": balanced,
        "class_function": class_function,
        "certified_ceiling_bits": ceiling,
        "H(conjugacy class)": H_class,
        "exact_deficit_bits": H_class - ceiling,
        "valid": surjective and balanced and class_function,
    }


def _entropy(counts: Sequence[int]) -> float:
    total: int = sum(counts)
    return -sum((c / total) * log2(c / total) for c in counts if c > 0)

def primes_up_to(limit: int) -> List[int]:
    sieve: List[bool] = [True] * (limit + 1)
    sieve[0:2] = [False, False]
    for i in range(2, int(limit ** 0.5) + 1):
        if sieve[i]:
            for j in range(i * i, limit + 1, i):
                sieve[j] = False
    return [i for i, ok in enumerate(sieve) if ok]


def cubic_split_type(coeffs: Tuple[int, int, int], p: int) -> str:
    """Type of x^3 + a x^2 + b x + c modulo p, from its number of roots."""
    a, b, c = coeffs
    roots: int = sum(1 for x in range(p) if (x * x * x + a * x * x + b * x + c) % p == 0)
    return {3: "111", 1: "12"}.get(roots, "3")


def entropy(counts: Sequence[int]) -> float:
    total: int = sum(counts)
    return -sum((n / total) * log2(n / total) for n in counts if n > 0)


def chebotarev_scan(
    coeffs: Tuple[int, int, int], discriminant: int, limit: int

    modulus: int = abs(discriminant)
    ps: List[int] = [p for p in primes_up_to(limit) if modulus % p != 0 and p != 2]
    types: List[str] = [cubic_split_type(coeffs, p) for p in ps]

    global_counts: Dict[str, int] = defaultdict(int)
    by_residue: Dict[int, Dict[str, int]] = defaultdict(lambda: defaultdict(int))
    for p, t in zip(ps, types):
        global_counts[t] += 1
        by_residue[p % modulus][t] += 1

    H_T: float = entropy(list(global_counts.values()))
    H_T_given_residue: float = sum(

        for block in by_residue.values()

    mixed: List[int] = sorted(r for r, block in by_residue.items() if len(block) > 1)
    return {
        "primes": n,
        "densities": {t: c / n for t, c in sorted(global_counts.items())},
        "H(T)": H_T,
        "H(T | residue)": H_T_given_residue,
        "I(residue ; T)": H_T - H_T_given_residue,
        "mixed_residue_classes": mixed,
        "number_of_mixed_classes": len(mixed),

### A guided tour of how much a residue can tell you about a prime

---

## 0. The question in one picture

Pick a polynomial with integer coefficients — say the cubic

$$f(x) = x^3 + x + 1.$$

Over the rationals it is irreducible. Modulo a prime $p$ it usually is not: it may split into three linear factors (type **111**), into a linear times a quadratic (type **12**), or stay irreducible (type **3**). Which of the three happens looks, at first glance, like pure chaos.

It is not chaos. It is a **fair draw from a group**. The Galois group of $f$ is the symmetric group $S_3$ on the three roots, of order $6$, and the theorem of Chebotarev says the prime's *Frobenius element* — a permutation of the roots — is uniformly distributed over $S_3$. The splitting type is just its cycle type:

$$\Pr[\texttt{111}] = \tfrac16, \qquad \Pr[\texttt{12}] = \tfrac12, \qquad \Pr[\texttt{3}] = \tfrac13.$$

Our question: **how much of this can you predict from $p$ alone, without factoring anything?**

<details>
<summary><b>New to Frobenius elements? Click for a two-minute primer.</b></summary>

For a prime $p$ not dividing the discriminant, reducing $f$ mod $p$ and factoring it gives a partition of $\deg f$ by the degrees of the factors. Inside the splitting field, raising to the $p$-th power is a field automorphism — the *Frobenius* — and its action permutes the roots of $f$. Its cycle lengths are exactly the degrees of the irreducible factors mod $p$. Changing the choice of prime above $p$ conjugates the permutation, so what is canonically attached to $p$ is a **conjugacy class**, and for $S_n$ a conjugacy class *is* a cycle type. See [Chebotarev's density theorem](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Chebotarev%27s_density_theorem) for the equidistribution statement.

</details>

---

## 1. Play with it first

Before any theory: choose a Galois group, choose what you are allowed to see about a prime, and watch the bits move. The green bar is the information you gain; the yellow line is the ceiling we are going to prove.

{{interactive_demo:0}}

Two things to try:

* Select **the quadratic character (sign)** — the green bar lands exactly on $1.000000$, on the yellow line. Not $0.99$, not $1.01$. Exactly one bit.
* Select **"does $p$ split completely?"** — a perfectly reasonable question, and it collapses to $0.1908$ bits. Coarser questions do strictly worse.
* Switch to $S_4$ and $S_5$: the total entropy climbs, and the green bar stays pinned at exactly one bit.

---

## 2. What "one bit" means, precisely

Uncertainty is measured in bits by Shannon's entropy $H = -\sum_i p_i\log_2 p_i$. For our cubic,

$$H(T) = -\tfrac16\log_2\tfrac16 - \tfrac12\log_2\tfrac12 - \tfrac13\log_2\tfrac13 = \frac23 + \frac{\log_2 3}{2} = 1.4591\ldots$$

The cheap prediction available since the nineteenth century is the **quadratic character** of the discriminant. Here $\operatorname{disc}(f) = -31$, and the Legendre symbol $\left(\frac{-31}{p}\right)$ — computable from $p \bmod 31$ alone, by quadratic reciprocity — equals the **sign** of the Frobenius permutation:

$$\left(\tfrac{-31}{p}\right) = \begin{cases}-1 & \text{type } \texttt{12} \text{ (a transposition: odd)}\\ +1 & \text{type } \texttt{111} \text{ or } \texttt{3} \text{ (identity or 3-cycle: even)}\end{cases}$$

Condition on it. If the symbol is $-1$ you know the type exactly: $\texttt{12}$, zero residual uncertainty. If it is $+1$ you are left with a biased coin, $\texttt{111}$ with probability $\tfrac13$ and $\texttt{3}$ with probability $\tfrac23$. Hence

$$H(T\mid \text{sign}) = \tfrac12\cdot 0 + \tfrac12\Big(\log_2 3 - \tfrac23\Big) = \frac{\log_2 3}{2} - \frac13 = 0.4591\ldots$$

and the **mutual information** — the bits the character buys you — is

$$I(T;\text{sign}) = 1.4591\ldots - 0.4591\ldots = 1 \quad\textbf{exactly.}$$

<details>
<summary><b>Why is the answer an exact integer, when both entropies are irrational?</b></summary>

Mutual information is symmetric: $I(T;S) = I(S;T)$. So instead of asking how much the character says about the type, ask how much the type says about the character — and the answer is *everything*, because the sign is a function of the cycle type. So $H(S\mid T)=0$ and

$$I(T;S) = H(S) - H(S\mid T) = H(S).$$

The sign is a **fair** coin on $S_3$ (three even elements, three odd), so $H(S)=1$. The $\log_2 3$ terms cancel because they measure the same hidden $1:2$ coin on both sides of the ledger. This argument uses nothing about $31$, nothing about cubics — which is why it generalizes so far.

</details>

---

## 3. The general theorem: the abelian ceiling

Let $G$ be any finite group and $\chi : G \to C$ **any** surjective homomorphism onto a finite **abelian** group. Write $\mathrm{cl}$ for the conjugacy-class read-out of a uniformly random element.

> **Theorem (exact visible information).** $I(\mathrm{cl};\chi) = \log_2\lvert C\rvert$.
>
> **Theorem (the ceiling).** For every map $u$, $\;I(\mathrm{cl}; u\circ\chi) \le \log_2\lvert C\rvert$, with equality at $u = \mathrm{id}$.
>
> **Theorem (the deficit).** $H(\mathrm{cl}\mid\chi) = H(\mathrm{cl}) - \log_2\lvert C\rvert$.

<details>
<summary><b>Click to reveal the proofs — they are three lines each.</b></summary>

*Exactness.* A homomorphism into an abelian group is a class function: $\chi(cxc^{-1}) = \chi(c)\chi(x)\chi(c)^{-1} = \chi(x)$. So the conjugacy class always determines $\chi$, giving $H(\chi\mid\mathrm{cl})=0$ with **no hypothesis at all**. And every fibre of a surjective homomorphism is a coset of the kernel, so all $\lvert C\rvert$ fibres have size $\lvert G\rvert/\lvert C\rvert$ — a perfectly balanced read-out, whose entropy is $\log_2\lvert C\rvert$. By symmetry, $I(\mathrm{cl};\chi) = H(\chi) - H(\chi\mid\mathrm{cl}) = \log_2\lvert C\rvert$. $\blacksquare$

*Ceiling.* $I(\mathrm{cl};u\circ\chi)\le H(u\circ\chi)$ (information about a variable never exceeds its entropy) and $H(u\circ\chi)\le H(\chi)$ (post-processing merges fibres, and merging fibres never increases entropy). Chain the two. $\blacksquare$

*Deficit.* Rearrange $I = H(\mathrm{cl}) - H(\mathrm{cl}\mid\chi)$. $\blacksquare$

</details>

**Why this is a statement about primes.** Class field theory says that the read-outs of the Frobenius that are *congruence conditions on $p$* are exactly the ones factoring through the abelianization $G^{\mathrm{ab}} = G/[G,G]$. So the ceiling reads:

> No congruence on $p$, of any modulus, reveals more than $\log_2\lvert G^{\mathrm{ab}}\rvert$ bits about how $p$ factors.

For our cubic $G^{\mathrm{ab}} = C_2$, ceiling $= 1$ bit, attained by the Legendre symbol. For an **abelian** Galois group, $G^{\mathrm{ab}} = G$ and the residue determines everything — that is [quadratic reciprocity](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Quadratic_reciprocity), read as an information statement. For a **perfect** group like $A_5$, the ceiling is $0$: congruences say nothing whatsoever.

---

## 5. Now look at actual primes

Theory says the residue class of $p$ modulo $31$ is worth exactly one bit — no more than the single symbol $\left(\frac{-31}{p}\right)$. Here is the experiment: sieve the primes, factor the cubic modulo each, sort by residue, and watch.

{{interactive_demo:1}}

Slide the bound up and note two things:

1. **The measured $I(p \bmod 31;\text{type})$ converges to $1$**, not to $1.4591$. Knowing the full residue is worth no more than knowing the one bit of parity.
2. **Exactly $15$ of the $30$ residue classes are "mixed"** — they contain primes of type $\texttt{111}$ *and* primes of type $\texttt{3}$. Those $15$ are precisely the quadratic residues mod $31$.

<details>
<summary><b>Are the mixed classes a bug in the experiment?</b></summary>

No — they are the theorem, made countable. The character separates even from odd, and nothing else. Inside the even half of $S_3$ sit the identity (type $\texttt{111}$, one element) and the two three-cycles (type $\texttt{3}$), a $1:2$ split that is *identical in every even residue class*. ## 8. Where the missing bits actually live

The $0.4591$ hidden bits are not lost; they are *elsewhere*. For this cubic, the Frobenius gives a two-dimensional Galois representation, and the coefficients $a_p$ of the associated weight-one cusp form distinguish the identity class ($a_p = 2$) from the three-cycles ($a_p = -1$) — precisely the distinction no residue can make. That is the pattern the [Langlands program](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Langlands_program) generalizes: when congruences run out of information, modular forms supply the rest.

### Open questions this raises

* **Rigidity.** Is the ceiling attained *only* by read-outs from which the character can be reconstructed? The proof suggests yes, but a quantitative gap $\log_2\lvert C\rvert - I \ge c\cdot(\text{defect})$ is missing.
* **A closed form for $S_n$.** The cycle-type distribution is the Ewens measure at parameter $1$, $\Pr[\lambda] = 1/z_\lambda$ with $z_\lambda = \prod_i i^{m_i}m_i!$. What is $H(T)$ in closed form, and at what rate does $H(T)-1$ diverge?
* **Composita.** For coprime discriminants, $(G_1\times G_2)^{\mathrm{ab}} = G_1^{\mathrm{ab}}\times G_2^{\mathrm{ab}}$, so visible bits should add while total entropy is subadditive: the hidden fraction grows under composition.

---

### One sentence to take away

The number of bits the world will show you about a prime's factorization is the logarithm of the size of an abelian quotient — for the cubic $x^3+x+1$ that is $\log_2 2 = 1$, and the remaining $0.4591$ bits are locked behind non-commutativity itself.

namespace CyclicTypeChannel

open Finset

variable {α β γ : Type*}

/-! ## 1. The chain rule and the symmetry of mutual information

The counting entropies of `Catalog.Shared.CyclicTypeChannel` satisfy the full Shannon calculus.
The two facts we need — the chain rule and the symmetry `I(g;k) = I(k;g)` — are proved here from
scratch; symmetry is what converts the (hard) statement "the type tells you the character" into
the (easy) statement "the character is a function of the type". -/

section ChainRule

variable [DecidableEq β] [DecidableEq γ] {s : Finset α} {g : α → β} {k : α → γ}

/-- A read-out that is constant on `s` carries no entropy. -/
lemma uEnt_eq_zero_of_const (hconst : ∀ x ∈ s, ∀ y ∈ s, g x = g y) : uEnt s g = 0 := by
  classical
  rcases s.eq_empty_or_nonempty with rfl | hs
  · simp [uEnt]
  have hfib : ∀ a ∈ s, {x ∈ s | g x = g a} = s := by
    intro a ha
    apply Finset.filter_true_of_mem
    intro x hx
    exact hconst x hx a ha
  have hN : (0 : ℝ) < s.card := by exact_mod_cast card_pos.2 hs
  have : ∑ a ∈ s, Real.logb 2 (#{x ∈ s | g x = g a} : ℝ)
      = (s.card : ℝ) * Real.logb 2 (s.card : ℝ) := by
    rw [Finset.sum_congr rfl (fun a ha => by rw [hfib a ha])]
    simp [Finset.sum_const, nsmul_eq_mul]
  rw [uEnt, this]
  field_simp
  ring

/-- The joint read-out does not care about the order of its two components. -/
lemma uEnt_joint_comm (s : Finset α) (g : α → β) (k : α → γ) :
    uEnt s (fun a => (g a, k a)) = uEnt s (fun a => (k a, g a)) := by
  classical
  have : ∀ a : α, {x ∈ s | (g x, k x) = (g a, k a)} = {x ∈ s | (k x, g x) = (k a, g a)} := by
    intro a
    apply Finset.filter_congr
    intro x _
    simp [Prod.ext_iff, and_comm]
  simp only [uEnt, this]

/-- **The chain rule** `H(g | k) = H(g, k) - H(k)`.  This is the identity that makes the counting
entropy of `uEnt` a genuine Shannon entropy rather than an ad-hoc average. -/
theorem condEnt_eq_joint_sub (hs : s.Nonempty) (g : α → β) (k : α → γ) :
    condEnt s g k = uEnt s (fun a => (g a, k a)) - uEnt s k := by
  classical
  have hN : (0 : ℝ) < s.card := by exact_mod_cast card_pos.2 hs
  -- each conditional term is a difference of two sums over the fibre
  have hterm : ∀ c ∈ s.image k,
      ((#{x ∈ s | k x = c} : ℝ) / s.card) * uEnt {x ∈ s | k x = c} g
        = ((#{x ∈ s | k x = c} : ℝ) / s.card) * Real.logb 2 (#{x ∈ s | k x = c} : ℝ)
          - (∑ a ∈ {x ∈ s | k x = c},
              Real.logb 2 (#{x ∈ s | (g x, k x) = (g a, k a)} : ℝ)) / s.card := by
    intro c hc
    obtain ⟨a₀, ha₀, rfl⟩ := mem_image.1 hc
    set t : Finset α := {x ∈ s | k x = k a₀} with ht
    have htne : t.Nonempty := ⟨a₀, by simp [ht, ha₀]⟩
    have hn : (0 : ℝ) < t.card := by exact_mod_cast card_pos.2 htne
    -- inner fibres of `g` inside `t` are the joint fibres inside `s`
    have hfib : ∀ a ∈ t, {x ∈ t | g x = g a} = {x ∈ s | (g x, k x) = (g a, k a)} := by
      intro a ha
      have hka : k a = k a₀ := by simpa [ht] using (mem_filter.1 ha).2
      ext x
      simp only [ht, mem_filter, Prod.ext_iff]
      constructor
      · rintro ⟨⟨hxs, hxk⟩, hxg⟩; exact ⟨hxs, hxg, by rw [hxk, hka]⟩
      · rintro ⟨hxs, hxg, hxk⟩; exact ⟨⟨hxs, by rw [hxk, hka]⟩, hxg⟩
    have hn' : (t.card : ℝ) ≠ 0 := ne_of_gt hn
    have hN' : ((s.card : ℝ)) ≠ 0 := ne_of_gt hN
    rw [uEnt, Finset.sum_congr rfl (fun a ha => by rw [hfib a ha])]
    field_simp
  rw [condEnt, Finset.sum_congr rfl hterm, Finset.sum_sub_distrib]
  -- the first part reassembles into the `k`-entropy sum, the second into the joint sum
  have h1 : ∑ c ∈ s.image k,
      ((#{x ∈ s | k x = c} : ℝ) / s.card) * Real.logb 2 (#{x ∈ s | k x = c} : ℝ)
      = (∑ a ∈ s, Real.logb 2 (#{x ∈ s | k x = k a} : ℝ)) / s.card := by
    rw [sum_logb_fiber, Finset.sum_div]
    exact Finset.sum_congr rfl fun v _ => by ring
  have h2 : ∑ c ∈ s.image k,
      (∑ a ∈ {x ∈ s | k x = c},
        Real.logb 2 (#{x ∈ s | (g x, k x) = (g a, k a)} : ℝ)) / s.card
      = (∑ a ∈ s, Real.logb 2 (#{x ∈ s | (g x, k x) = (g a, k a)} : ℝ)) / s.card := by
    rw [← Finset.sum_div]
    congr 1
    exact Finset.sum_fiberwise_of_maps_to (fun x hx => mem_image_of_mem k hx) _
  rw [h1, h2, uEnt, uEnt]
  ring

/-- **Symmetry of mutual information.** -/
theorem mutInfo_comm (hs : s.Nonempty) (g : α → β) (k : α → γ) :
    mutInfo s g k = mutInfo s k g := by
  rw [mutInfo, mutInfo, condEnt_eq_joint_sub hs g k, condEnt_eq_joint_sub hs k g,
    uEnt_joint_comm s k g]
  ring

/-- Conditional entropy is non-negative. -/
theorem condEnt_nonneg (s : Finset α) (g : α → β) (k : α → γ) : 0 ≤ condEnt s g k := by
  refine Finset.sum_nonneg fun c _ => ?_
  have h₁ : (0 : ℝ) ≤ (#{x ∈ s | k x = c} : ℝ) / s.card := by positivity
  exact mul_nonneg h₁ (uEnt_nonneg _ _)

/-- **The cap.**  A read-out can never reveal more about `k` than `k` itself contains:
`I(g ; k) ≤ H(k)`.  For a balanced binary character this is the one-bit ceiling. -/
theorem mutInfo_le_uEnt_right (hs : s.Nonempty) (g : α → β) (k : α → γ) :
    mutInfo s g k ≤ uEnt s k := by
  rw [mutInfo_comm hs, mutInfo]
  linarith [condEnt_nonneg s k g]

/-- Mutual information is bounded by the entropy of the read-out itself. -/
theorem mutInfo_le_uEnt_left (s : Finset α) (g : α → β) (k : α → γ) :
    mutInfo s g k ≤ uEnt s g := by
  rw [mutInfo]
  linarith [condEnt_nonneg s g k]

end ChainRule

/-! ## 2. Balanced binary read-outs and the one-bit theorem -/

section OneBit

variable [DecidableEq β] [DecidableEq γ] {s : Finset α} {g : α → β} {k : α → γ}

/-- **A balanced binary read-out carries exactly one bit.**  "Balanced" is expressed without
mentioning the two values: every fibre is exactly half of `s`. -/
theorem uEnt_eq_one_of_balanced (hs : s.Nonempty)
    (hbal : ∀ a ∈ s, 2 * #{x ∈ s | k x = k a} = s.card) : uEnt s k = 1 := by
  classical
  have hN : (0 : ℝ) < s.card := by exact_mod_cast card_pos.2 hs
  have hterm : ∀ a ∈ s, Real.logb 2 (#{x ∈ s | k x = k a} : ℝ)
      = Real.logb 2 (s.card : ℝ) - 1 := by
    intro a ha
    have h : (#{x ∈ s | k x = k a} : ℝ) = (s.card : ℝ) / 2 := by
      have := hbal a ha
      have : (2 : ℝ) * (#{x ∈ s | k x = k a} : ℝ) = (s.card : ℝ) := by exact_mod_cast this
      linarith
    rw [h, Real.logb_div (ne_of_gt hN) (by norm_num),
      Real.logb_self_eq_one (by norm_num : (1 : ℝ) < 2)]
  rw [uEnt, Finset.sum_congr rfl hterm]
  rw [Finset.sum_const, nsmul_eq_mul]
  field_simp
  ring

/-- If the read-out `g` refines `k` on `s` (equal `g`-values force equal `k`-values), then
knowing `g` determines `k`: `H(k | g) = 0`. -/
theorem condEnt_eq_zero_of_refines
    (href : ∀ x ∈ s, ∀ y ∈ s, g x = g y → k x = k y) : condEnt s k g = 0 := by
  classical
  refine Finset.sum_eq_zero fun v hv => ?_
  have : uEnt {x ∈ s | g x = v} k = 0 := by
    refine uEnt_eq_zero_of_const fun x hx y hy => ?_
    simp only [mem_filter] at hx hy
    exact href x hx.1 y hy.1 (by rw [hx.2, hy.2])
  rw [this, mul_zero]

/-- **The character captures exactly one bit.**

If the read-out `g` refines a balanced binary read-out `k`, then the channel from `g` to `k`
transmits exactly one bit — independently of how rich `g` itself is. -/
theorem mutInfo_eq_one_of_refines_balanced (hs : s.Nonempty)
    (href : ∀ x ∈ s, ∀ y ∈ s, g x = g y → k x = k y)
    (hbal : ∀ a ∈ s, 2 * #{x ∈ s | k x = k a} = s.card) :
    mutInfo s g k = 1 := by
  rw [mutInfo_comm hs, mutInfo, condEnt_eq_zero_of_refines href, sub_zero,
    uEnt_eq_one_of_balanced hs hbal]

/-- **The locked residual.**  Under the same hypotheses the conditional entropy of the type given
the character is exactly `H(T) - 1`: whatever the type knows beyond one bit stays hidden. -/
theorem condEnt_eq_uEnt_sub_one (hs : s.Nonempty)
    (href : ∀ x ∈ s, ∀ y ∈ s, g x = g y → k x = k y)
    (hbal : ∀ a ∈ s, 2 * #{x ∈ s | k x = k a} = s.card) :
    condEnt s g k = uEnt s g - 1 := by
  have h := mutInfo_eq_one_of_refines_balanced hs href hbal
  rw [mutInfo] at h
  linarith

end OneBit

/-! ## 2b. Strict positivity: when a read-out really does hide something -/

section StrictPos

variable [DecidableEq β] [DecidableEq γ] {s t : Finset α} {g : α → β} {k : α → γ}

/-- **A non-constant read-out has strictly positive entropy.**  This is the quantitative form of
"the fibres are proper subsets": every fibre misses one of the two witnesses, so every fibre
logarithm is at most `log₂ (|t| - 1)`. -/
theorem uEnt_pos_of_ne {x y : α} (hx : x ∈ t) (hy : y ∈ t) (hne : k x ≠ k y) : 0 < uEnt t k := by
  classical
  have hxy : x ≠ y := fun h => hne (by rw [h])
  have hN2 : 2 ≤ t.card := Finset.one_lt_card.2 ⟨x, hx, y, hy, hxy⟩
  have hN : (0 : ℝ) < t.card := by
    have : 0 < t.card := by omega
    exact_mod_cast this
  have hNm : (0 : ℝ) < (t.card : ℝ) - 1 := by
    have : (2 : ℝ) ≤ (t.card : ℝ) := by exact_mod_cast hN2
    linarith
  have hterm : ∀ a ∈ t, Real.logb 2 (#{z ∈ t | k z = k a} : ℝ)
      ≤ Real.logb 2 ((t.card : ℝ) - 1) := by
    intro a ha
    have hlt : #{z ∈ t | k z = k a} < t.card := by
      by_cases hax : k a = k x
      · refine Finset.card_lt_card ⟨Finset.filter_subset _ _, fun hsub => ?_⟩
        have : y ∈ {z ∈ t | k z = k a} := hsub hy
        rw [Finset.mem_filter] at this
        exact hne (by rw [← hax, this.2])
      · refine Finset.card_lt_card ⟨Finset.filter_subset _ _, fun hsub => ?_⟩
        have : x ∈ {z ∈ t | k z = k a} := hsub hx
        rw [Finset.mem_filter] at this
        exact hax this.2.symm
    have hpos : (0 : ℝ) < (#{z ∈ t | k z = k a} : ℝ) := by
      exact_mod_cast fiber_card_pos ha
    have hle : (#{z ∈ t | k z = k a} : ℝ) ≤ (t.card : ℝ) - 1 := by
      have : (#{z ∈ t | k z = k a} : ℕ) + 1 ≤ t.card := hlt
      have : ((#{z ∈ t | k z = k a} : ℕ) : ℝ) + 1 ≤ (t.card : ℝ) := by exact_mod_cast this
      linarith
    exact Real.logb_le_logb_of_le (by norm_num) hpos hle
  have hsum : (∑ a ∈ t, Real.logb 2 (#{z ∈ t | k z = k a} : ℝ))
      ≤ (t.card : ℝ) * Real.logb 2 ((t.card : ℝ) - 1) := by
    calc (∑ a ∈ t, Real.logb 2 (#{z ∈ t | k z = k a} : ℝ))
        ≤ ∑ _a ∈ t, Real.logb 2 ((t.card : ℝ) - 1) := Finset.sum_le_sum hterm
      _ = (t.card : ℝ) * Real.logb 2 ((t.card : ℝ) - 1) := by
          simp [Finset.sum_const, nsmul_eq_mul]
  have hstrict : Real.logb 2 ((t.card : ℝ) - 1) < Real.logb 2 (t.card : ℝ) :=
    Real.logb_lt_logb (by norm_num) hNm (by linarith)
  rw [uEnt, sub_pos, div_lt_iff₀ hN]
  calc (∑ a ∈ t, Real.logb 2 (#{z ∈ t | k z = k a} : ℝ))
      ≤ (t.card : ℝ) * Real.logb 2 ((t.card : ℝ) - 1) := hsum
    _ < Real.logb 2 (t.card : ℝ) * (t.card : ℝ) := by nlinarith [hstrict, hN]

/-- **A conditioning variable that leaves a fibre mixed has strictly positive conditional
entropy.**  This is what makes the one-bit theorem non-vacuous: without the refinement hypothesis
the mutual information genuinely drops below the ceiling. -/
theorem condEnt_pos_of_fiber_ne {x y : α} (hx : x ∈ s) (hy : y ∈ s)
    (hg : g x = g y) (hk : k x ≠ k y) : 0 < condEnt s k g := by
  classical
  have hsne : s.Nonempty := ⟨x, hx⟩
  have hN : (0 : ℝ) < s.card := by exact_mod_cast card_pos.2 hsne
  refine Finset.sum_pos' (fun c _ => ?_) ⟨g x, mem_image_of_mem g hx, ?_⟩
  · exact mul_nonneg (by positivity) (uEnt_nonneg _ _)
  · have hxmem : x ∈ {z ∈ s | g z = g x} := by simp [hx]
    have hymem : y ∈ {z ∈ s | g z = g x} := by simp [hy, hg]
    have hw : (0 : ℝ) < (#{z ∈ s | g z = g x} : ℝ) / s.card := by
      have : (0 : ℝ) < (#{z ∈ s | g z = g x} : ℝ) := by
        exact_mod_cast Finset.card_pos.2 ⟨x, hxmem⟩
      positivity
    exact mul_pos hw (uEnt_pos_of_ne hxmem hymem hk)

end StrictPos

/-! ## 3. The group form: `G^ab = C₂` gives exactly one bit

Chebotarev makes the Frobenius class equidistributed in `G`, so the uniform counting measure on
`G` *is* the density measure on primes.  A residue `p mod |disc|` sees the Frobenius only through
the abelian quotient; when that quotient has order two, the visible datum is a single surjective
character `χ : G →* C` with `|C| = 2`, and the splitting type determines it. -/

section GroupForm

/-- The canonical map to the abelianization is surjective. -/
theorem abelianization_of_surjective {G : Type*} [Group G] :
    Function.Surjective (Abelianization.of : G → Abelianization G) := by
  intro x
  induction x using QuotientGroup.induction_on with
  | H g => exact ⟨g, rfl⟩

variable {G C : Type*} [Group G] [Fintype G] [Group C] [Fintype C] [DecidableEq C]

/-- Every fibre of a surjective character onto a two-element group is exactly half of the group. -/
theorem card_fiber_character (χ : G →* C) (hsurj : Function.Surjective χ)
    (hC : Fintype.card C = 2) (a : G) :
    2 * #{x : G | χ x = χ a} = Fintype.card G := by
  classical
  have hsum : Fintype.card G = ∑ c : C, #{x : G | χ x = c} :=
    Finset.card_eq_sum_card_fiberwise (fun x _ => Finset.mem_univ (χ x))
  have hconst : ∀ c : C, #{x : G | χ x = c} = #{x : G | χ x = χ a} :=
    fun c => MonoidHom.card_fiber_eq_of_mem_range χ (hsurj c) ⟨a, rfl⟩
  rw [hsum, Finset.sum_congr rfl fun c _ => hconst c, Finset.sum_const, Finset.card_univ, hC,
    smul_eq_mul]

/-- **`G^ab = C₂` ⟹ exactly one bit.**  For any finite group `G`, any surjective character
`χ : G →* C` onto a two-element group, and any splitting-type read-out `T` through which `χ`
factors, the type/character channel carries exactly one bit.  Nothing about `G` beyond the
existence of the index-two kernel is used — this is the promised uniformity over all `S₃`, `S₄`
and `S₅` fields. -/
theorem mutInfo_character_eq_one {β : Type*} [DecidableEq β] (T : G → β) (χ : G →* C)
    (hsurj : Function.Surjective χ) (hC : Fintype.card C = 2)
    (f : β → C) (hf : ∀ x : G, χ x = f (T x)) :
    mutInfo (univ : Finset G) T (fun x => χ x) = 1 := by
  classical
  have hne : (univ : Finset G).Nonempty := univ_nonempty
  refine mutInfo_eq_one_of_refines_balanced hne (fun x _ y _ hxy => ?_) (fun a _ => ?_)
  · rw [hf x, hf y, hxy]
  · rw [Finset.card_univ]
    exact card_fiber_character χ hsurj hC a

/-- The same statement with the abelianization in place of an abstract character: if `G^ab` has
order two and the type read-out determines the image in `G^ab`, the channel is one bit. -/
theorem mutInfo_abelianization_eq_one {β : Type*} [DecidableEq β]
    [Fintype (Abelianization G)] [DecidableEq (Abelianization G)]
    (T : G → β) (hC : Fintype.card (Abelianization G) = 2)
    (f : β → Abelianization G) (hf : ∀ x : G, Abelianization.of x = f (T x)) :
    mutInfo (univ : Finset G) T (fun x => Abelianization.of x) = 1 :=
  mutInfo_character_eq_one T (Abelianization.of) abelianization_of_surjective hC f hf

    mutInfo (univ : Finset (Perm (Fin 3))) (fun σ => ConjClasses.mk σ)
        (fun σ => Equiv.Perm.sign σ) = 1 :=
  mutInfo_conjClasses_eq_one_of_card_two (fun a b => mul_comm a b) Equiv.Perm.sign
    sign_surjective_three (by simp)

function of `p mod 31` that is visible in the abelian quotient — is capped at one bit. -/

  "future_directions": "# Future Directions — after "the character captures exactly one bit"

The cycle closed the target claim and then generalised past it: the one bit is log₂ 2, and the
theorem is I(Frobenius class ; χ) = log₂ |C| for every surjective character χ : G → C into a
finite abelian group, with log₂ |C| also a *ceiling* for every read-out that factors through χ.
The open questions below are what the proofs did **not** settle.

## C1. Equality-case rigidity for the abelian ceiling

**Conjecture.** Let G be a finite group, χ : G → C a surjective character into an abelian
group, and w a read-out of the Frobenius class. Then I(class ; w) = log₂ |C| **iff** w separates
the fibres of χ (i.e. χ is a function of w almost everywhere). Equivalently, the ceiling is
attained only by read-outs that recover the character.

*The key insight is* that the ceiling proof factors as I ≤ H(w) ≤ H(χ) = log₂ |C|, and both
inequalities are equalities exactly when the corresponding conditional entropies vanish — so
rigidity is a statement about strict concavity of −p log p, not about arithmetic.

*Why now?* The strict-positivity machinery needed for the "only if" half already exists (a
non-constant read-out has strictly positive entropy; a conditioning variable that leaves a fibre
mixed has strictly positive conditional entropy), and the "if" half is the exact-information
theorem. Only the quantitative gap log₂ |C| − I ≥ c · (defect) is missing.

## C2. The exact residual for Sₙ: H(T) − 1 in closed form

**Conjecture.** For every n ≥ 2 the residual entropy of the cycle type given the sign is
H(T | sign) = H(T) − 1, and H(T) equals the entropy of the partition distribution
p(λ) = 1 / z_λ with z_λ = ∏ i^{m_i} m_i!; consequently
H(T) = log₂ n! − (1/n!) ∑_{λ ⊢ n} (n!/z_λ) log₂ (n!/z_λ) and H(T) − 1 → ∞ at rate Θ(log n).

*The key insight is* that 1/z_λ is a probability distribution on partitions independent of the
sign conditioning, so the entire non-abelian residual is the entropy of the Cauchy/Ewens measure at
parameter 1.

*Why now?* The one-bit law for all symmetric groups already gives H(T | sign) = H(T) − 1 for every
n; what remains is the closed form of H(T) itself, for which the standard cycle-type counting is
available.

## C3. Multiplicativity of the visible bits over composita

**Conjecture.** For number fields K₁, K₂ with Galois groups G₁, G₂ and coprime discriminants,
the compositum has I(class ; residue) = log₂ |G₁^ab| + log₂ |G₂^ab|; the visible information is
additive while the total type entropy is *sub*additive, so the hidden fraction grows.

*The key insight is* that (G₁ × G₂)^ab = G₁^ab × G₂^ab, so the abelian ceiling is additive for the
entropy of a product read-out, whereas conjugacy classes multiply only up to the class-fusion of the
product group.

*Why now?* A Chinese-remainder/product law for the cyclic type channel is already available, so the
additive half of the statement is within reach; the subadditivity of the type entropy under
composition is the remaining input.

## C4. Noisy read-outs and sufficient statistics

Replacing the deterministic post-processing u ∘ χ by an arbitrary Markov kernel would place the
ceiling in the setting of the general data-processing inequality. The bound log₂ |G^ab| should
persist, and the equality case should become the statement that the character is a sufficient
statistic for the residue-visible information.

## C5. Large deviations for residue-stratified scans

Beyond entropy, the full distribution of log-likelihood ratios between residue-conditional and
unconditional type distributions is computable in closed form for Sₙ. Large-deviation rates for
"how atypical can a residue class look at height X" would turn the empirical scans into sharp
statistical tests of the ceiling.

  "modules": {
    "demo": "#!/usr/bin/env python3
"""
The abelian ceiling: exactly log2 |G^ab| bits of Frobenius information
are visible in a residue.

This self-contained script demonstrates, numerically and by exhaustive
enumeration, every quantitative claim of the accompanying paper:

  1. The Chebotarev channel of the cubic field x^3 + x + 1 (discriminant -31,
     Galois group S_3):  H(T) = 2/3 + (log2 3)/2 = 1.4591...,
     H(T | sign) = (log2 3)/2 - 1/3 = 0.4591..., I(T ; sign) = 1 EXACTLY.

  2. The decomposition H(T | sign) = (1/2) * H(1/3, 2/3):  the odd half of the
     group is pure, the even half splits 1 : 2.

  3. The abelian ceiling: for every surjective character chi : G -> C onto a
     finite abelian group, I(conjugacy class ; chi) = log2 |C|, and every
     post-processing u . chi satisfies I <= log2 |C| (checked by brute-force
     enumeration of ALL set partitions of C).

  4. The dichotomy: an abelian Galois group hides nothing (I = log2 |G|);
     a symmetric group leaks exactly one bit for every n >= 2.

  5. An honest arithmetic scan: factorization types of x^3 + x + 1 modulo the
     primes, stratified by residue mod 31, exhibiting the 15 mixed-type
     residue classes forced by the theory.

Run:  python3 demo.py
Only the standard library is used.
"""

from __future__ import annotations

from collections import Counter, defaultdict
from itertools import permutations
from math import log2
from typing import Callable, Dict, Hashable, Iterable, List, Sequence, Tuple

Perm = Tuple[int, ...]
Readout = Callable[[Perm], Hashable]


# ----------------------------------------------------------------------
# 1. The counting-entropy calculus (uniform / Chebotarev measure)
# ----------------------------------------------------------------------

def entropy_of_counts(counts: Iterable[int]) -> float:
    """Shannon entropy in bits of the distribution proportional to `counts`."""
    cs: List[int] = [c for c in counts if c > 0]
    total: int = sum(cs)
    if total == 0:
        return 0.0
    return -sum((c / total) * log2(c / total) for c in cs)


def uniform_entropy(domain: Sequence[Hashable], g: Callable[[Hashable], Hashable]) -> float:
    """H(g) for the uniform measure on `domain`."""
    return entropy_of_counts(Counter(g(x) for x in domain).values())


def conditional_entropy(
    domain: Sequence[Hashable],
    g: Callable[[Hashable], Hashable],
    k: Callable[[Hashable], Hashable],
) -> float:
    """H(g | k): the average entropy of g over the fibres of k."""
    blocks: Dict[Hashable, List[Hashable]] = defaultdict(list)
    for x in domain:
        blocks[k(x)].append(x)
    n: int = len(domain)
    return sum((len(b) / n) * uniform_entropy(b, g) for b in blocks.values())


def mutual_information(
    domain: Sequence[Hashable],
    g: Callable[[Hashable], Hashable],
    k: Callable[[Hashable], Hashable],
) -> float:
    """I(g ; k) = H(g) - H(g | k)."""
    return uniform_entropy(domain, g) - conditional_entropy(domain, g, k)


# ----------------------------------------------------------------------
# 2. Permutation groups, cycle types, signs, conjugacy classes
# ----------------------------------------------------------------------

def symmetric_group(n: int) -> List[Perm]:
    """All permutations of {0,...,n-1}, as tuples p with i |-> p[i]."""
    return [tuple(p) for p in permutations(range(n))]


def cycle_type(p: Perm) -> Tuple[int, ...]:
    """Cycle type of p as a weakly decreasing tuple (a partition of n)."""
    n: int = len(p)
    seen: List[bool] = [False] * n
    parts: List[int] = []
    for i in range(n):
        if not seen[i]:
            length, j = 0, i
            while not seen[j]:
                seen[j] = True
                j = p[j]
                length += 1
            parts.append(length)
    return tuple(sorted(parts, reverse=True))


def sign(p: Perm) -> int:
    """Sign of a permutation: +1 if even, -1 if odd."""
    ct: Tuple[int, ...] = cycle_type(p)
    return (-1) ** sum(length - 1 for length in ct)


def conj_class(p: Perm) -> Tuple[int, ...]:
    """For a symmetric group, the conjugacy class is exactly the cycle type."""
    return cycle_type(p)


def type_label(ct: Tuple[int, ...]) -> str:
    """'111', '12', '3', ... — the classical splitting-type notation."""
    return "".join(str(part) for part in sorted(ct))


# ----------------------------------------------------------------------
# 3. Demonstration 1 — the S_3 cubic x^3 + x + 1, discriminant -31
# ----------------------------------------------------------------------

def demo_s3_channel() -> None:
    print("=" * 72)
    print("1. THE CUBIC x^3 + x + 1,  disc = -31,  Galois group S_3")
    print("=" * 72)

    G: List[Perm] = symmetric_group(3)
    counts: Counter = Counter(type_label(cycle_type(p)) for p in G)
    print("\nChebotarev densities (fraction of the group per splitting type):")
    for label in ("111", "12", "3"):
        print(f"   type {label:>3} : {counts[label]}/6 = {counts[label] / 6:.6f}")

    H_T: float = uniform_entropy(G, lambda p: cycle_type(p))
    H_sign: float = uniform_entropy(G, sign)
    H_T_given_sign: float = conditional_entropy(G, lambda p: cycle_type(p), sign)
    I: float = mutual_information(G, lambda p: cycle_type(p), sign)

    exact_H_T: float = 2 / 3 + log2(3) / 2
    exact_res: float = log2(3) / 2 - 1 / 3

    print(f"\n   H(T)              = {H_T:.10f}   (exact 2/3 + (log2 3)/2 = {exact_H_T:.10f})")
    print(f"   H(sign)           = {H_sign:.10f}   (a fair coin: 3 odd, 3 even)")
    print(f"   H(T | sign)       = {H_T_given_sign:.10f}   (exact (log2 3)/2 - 1/3 = {exact_res:.10f})")
    print(f"   I(T ; sign)       = {I:.10f}   <-- EXACTLY ONE BIT")
    print(f"   visible fraction  = {I / H_T:.4%}")

    assert abs(I - 1.0) < 1e-12
    assert abs(H_T - exact_H_T) < 1e-12
    assert abs(H_T_given_sign - exact_res) < 1e-12

    # symmetry of mutual information: the trivial direction
    H_sign_given_T: float = conditional_entropy(G, sign, lambda p: cycle_type(p))
    print(f"\n   H(sign | T)       = {H_sign_given_T:.10f}   (the sign IS a function of the type)")
    print("   hence  I(T ; sign) = I(sign ; T) = H(sign) - 0 = 1.")
    assert abs(H_sign_given_T) < 1e-12

    # the paper's decomposition
    half_binary: float = 0.5 * entropy_of_counts([1, 2])
    print(f"\n   Decomposition:  (1/2) * H(1/3, 2/3) = {half_binary:.10f}")
    print("   the odd half is pure (all type '12'); the even half splits 1 : 2.")
    assert abs(H_T_given_sign - half_binary) < 1e-12

    # strictness: a coarser read-out loses
    splits_completely: Readout = lambda p: cycle_type(p) == (1, 1, 1)
    I_coarse: float = mutual_information(G, splits_completely, sign)
    print(f"\n   Coarse read-out 'does p split completely?':  I = {I_coarse:.10f} < 1")
    print("   so the one-bit value is a property of the splitting type, not of the framework.")
    assert I_coarse < 1 - 1e-9


# ----------------------------------------------------------------------
# 4. Demonstration 2 — the abelian ceiling, verified by brute force
# ----------------------------------------------------------------------

def set_partitions(items: Sequence[Hashable]) -> Iterable[List[List[Hashable]]]:
    """All set partitions of `items` (Bell-number many)."""
    if not items:
        yield []
        return
    first, rest = items[0], items[1:]
    for partition in set_partitions(rest):
        for i in range(len(partition)):
            yield partition[:i] + [[first] + partition[i]] + partition[i + 1:]
        yield [[first]] + partition


def demo_abelian_ceiling(n: int = 4) -> None:
    print()
    print("=" * 72)
    print(f"2. THE ABELIAN CEILING for G = S_{n},  chi = sign,  C = {{+1,-1}}")
    print("=" * 72)

    G: List[Perm] = symmetric_group(n)
    ceiling: float = log2(2)

    I_exact: float = mutual_information(G, conj_class, sign)
    print(f"\n   I(conjugacy class ; sign) = {I_exact:.10f}   = log2 |C| = {ceiling:.10f}")
    assert abs(I_exact - ceiling) < 1e-12

    H_class: float = uniform_entropy(G, conj_class)
    deficit: float = conditional_entropy(G, conj_class, sign)
    print(f"   H(class)                  = {H_class:.10f}")
    print(f"   H(class | sign)           = {deficit:.10f}   = H(class) - log2 |C|")
    assert abs(deficit - (H_class - ceiling)) < 1e-12

    # every post-processing u of chi: enumerate ALL set partitions of C
    print("\n   Every read-out computed from the character (all set partitions of C):")
    for partition in set_partitions([1, -1]):
        lookup: Dict[int, int] = {}
        for idx, block in enumerate(partition):
            for value in block:
                lookup[value] = idx
        w: Readout = lambda p, lookup=lookup: lookup[sign(p)]
        I_w: float = mutual_information(G, conj_class, w)
        blocks_str: str = " | ".join("{" + ",".join(f"{v:+d}" for v in b) + "}" for b in partition)
        print(f"      u = {blocks_str:<20}  I = {I_w:.10f}  <= {ceiling:.6f}")
        assert I_w <= ceiling + 1e-12


def demo_dichotomy() -> None:
    print()
    print("=" * 72)
    print("3. THE DICHOTOMY: abelian groups hide nothing, S_n hides all but one bit")
    print("=" * 72)

    # abelian: the cyclic group Z/m under addition, conjugacy classes are singletons
    print("\n   Cyclic Galois group Z/m (e.g. a cyclic cubic or a cyclotomic field):")
    for m in (2, 3, 4, 6):
        elements: List[int] = list(range(m))
        I_ab: float = mutual_information(elements, lambda x: x, lambda x: x)
        print(f"      m = {m}:  I(class ; residue) = {I_ab:.6f} = log2 {m} = {log2(m):.6f}  (all of it)")
        assert abs(I_ab - log2(m)) < 1e-12

    print("\n   Symmetric Galois group S_n:")
    print("      n    H(cycle type)   I(type ; sign)   hidden bits   visible fraction")
    for n in range(2, 8):
        G: List[Perm] = symmetric_group(n)
        H_T: float = uniform_entropy(G, cycle_type)
        I: float = mutual_information(G, cycle_type, sign)
        print(f"      {n}    {H_T:13.6f}   {I:14.10f}   {H_T - I:11.6f}   {I / H_T:15.2%}")
        assert abs(I - 1.0) < 1e-12


# ----------------------------------------------------------------------
# 5. Demonstration 3 — an honest arithmetic scan
# ----------------------------------------------------------------------

def primes_up_to(limit: int) -> List[int]:
    """Sieve of Eratosthenes."""
    sieve: List[bool] = [True] * (limit + 1)
    sieve[0:2] = [False, False]
    for i in range(2, int(limit ** 0.5) + 1):
        if sieve[i]:
            for j in range(i * i, limit + 1, i):
                sieve[j] = False
    return [i for i, is_p in enumerate(sieve) if is_p]


def splitting_type_of_cubic(p: int) -> str:
    """
    Splitting type of x^3 + x + 1 modulo p, for p not dividing 31.

    A cubic over a finite field is determined by its number of roots:
      3 roots -> '111' (splits completely), 1 root -> '12', 0 roots -> '3'.
    """
    roots: int = sum(1 for x in range(p) if (x * x * x + x + 1) % p == 0)
    if roots == 3:
        return "111"
    if roots == 1:
        return "12"
    return "3"


def legendre_symbol(a: int, p: int) -> int:
    """The Legendre symbol (a|p) by Euler's criterion, p an odd prime."""
    a %= p
    if a == 0:
        return 0
    r: int = pow(a, (p - 1) // 2, p)
    return 1 if r == 1 else -1


def demo_prime_scan(limit: int = 20000) -> None:
    print()
    print("=" * 72)
    print(f"4. ARITHMETIC SCAN: x^3 + x + 1 modulo the primes p < {limit}")
    print("=" * 72)

    ps: List[int] = [p for p in primes_up_to(limit) if p != 31 and p != 2]
    types: List[str] = [splitting_type_of_cubic(p) for p in ps]
    counts: Counter = Counter(types)
    total: int = len(ps)

    print(f"\n   {total} primes scanned.")
    print("   type   observed density   Chebotarev prediction")
    for label, predicted in (("111", 1 / 6), ("12", 1 / 2), ("3", 1 / 3)):
        print(f"   {label:>4}   {counts[label] / total:16.6f}   {predicted:21.6f}")

    # the character really is the sign: (-31|p) = -1 exactly for type '12'
    mismatches: int = sum(
        1
        for p, t in zip(ps, types)
        if legendre_symbol(-31, p) != (-1 if t == "12" else 1)
    )
    print(f"\n   primes where (-31|p) disagrees with the parity of the type: {mismatches}")
    assert mismatches == 0

    # empirical entropies
    H_T: float = entropy_of_counts(counts.values())
    by_sign: Dict[int, Counter] = defaultdict(Counter)
    for p, t in zip(ps, types):
        by_sign[legendre_symbol(-31, p)][t] += 1
    H_T_given_sign: float = sum(
        (sum(c.values()) / total) * entropy_of_counts(c.values()) for c in by_sign.values()
    )
    print(f"\n   empirical H(T)        = {H_T:.6f}   (theory 1.459148)")
    print(f"   empirical H(T | sign) = {H_T_given_sign:.6f}   (theory 0.459148)")
    print(f"   empirical I           = {H_T - H_T_given_sign:.6f}   (theory 1.000000)")

    # residue stratification mod 31: which classes host more than one type?
    by_residue: Dict[int, set] = defaultdict(set)
    for p, t in zip(ps, types):
        by_residue[p % 31].add(t)
    mixed: List[int] = sorted(r for r, s in by_residue.items() if len(s) > 1)
    pure: List[int] = sorted(r for r, s in by_residue.items() if len(s) == 1)
    print(f"\n   residue classes mod 31 hosting >1 splitting type: {len(mixed)}")
    print(f"      {mixed}")
    print(f"   residue classes hosting exactly one type: {len(pure)}")
    print(f"      {pure}")
    print("\n   The mixed classes are exactly the 15 quadratic residues mod 31, i.e. the")
    print("   classes with (-31|p) = +1: the character separates even from odd and no")
    print("   more, so within the even classes the 1 : 2 split of identity vs 3-cycles")
    print("   is residue-independent.  These mixed classes ARE the 0.4591 hidden bits.")

    qrs: List[int] = sorted({(x * x) % 31 for x in range(1, 31)})
    assert mixed == qrs, (mixed, qrs)

    # empirical mutual information from the full residue, not just the sign
    I_residue: float = mutual_information(
        list(zip(ps, types)), lambda pt: pt[1], lambda pt: pt[0] % 31
    )
    print(f"\n   empirical I(p mod 31 ; type) = {I_residue:.6f}")
    print("   (finite-sample noise inflates this slightly above the exact value 1;")
    print("    the excess shrinks as the scan is extended)")


def main() -> None:
    demo_s3_channel()
    demo_abelian_ceiling(n=3)
    demo_abelian_ceiling(n=5)
    demo_dichotomy()
    demo_prime_scan(limit=20000)
    print()
    print("=" * 72)
    print("All assertions passed: the character captures exactly one bit, and the")
    print("abelian ceiling log2 |G^ab| is attained and never exceeded.")
    print("=" * 72)


if __name__ == "__main__":
    main()
